facts.text: The repository is a MuJoCo simulation environment for LimX humanoid robots (HU_D03, HU_D04) used to visualize models, test motion controllers and validate RL policies before deploying to hardware
The prerequisites are Linux x86_64; the bundled prebuild/kinematic_projection helper is x86_64-only and simulation functionality is limited on aarch64
The README installs the LimX motion control SDK wheel from limxsdk-lowlevel/python3/amd64
The available models are HU_D03_03 and HU_D04_01
The upstream loads the model with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(asset_path) and creates MjData from it
The upstream takes the actuator count from model.nu and the joint count from model.njnt
The upstream takes the integration step from model.opt.timestep
The upstream subscribes its simulation-side callback with robot.subscribeRobotCmdForSim
The simulation loop calls mujoco.mj_step(model, data) on every iteration
For the non-floating-base branch the upstream computes data.ctrl from the received RobotCmd as Kp * (q_cmd - q) + Kd * (dq_cmd - dq) + tau
The upstream publishes the robot state to the LimX SDK with publishRobotStateForSim
The upstream initializes the LimX SDK robot with robot.init(robot_ip) before starting the simulation
The upstream selects the model from the ROBOT_TYPE environment variable and passes it to SimulatorMujoco

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model file for the actuator control ranges and the qpos/qvel dimensions but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value, so trajectories, contacts, friction and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's
no mesh or texture of the model's asset directory is loaded by the stand-in and no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint of the model is resolved; the free base is not integrated
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

the upstream simulator exchanges RobotCmd, RobotState and ImuData with the LimX SDK (simulator.py:69, :132); this package exposes only the MuJoCo ctrl vector and integration state, not that topic layer
the upstream viewer, the kinematic_projection helper and the virtual joystick are not part of this driver; it has no rendering
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against the HU_D03 hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
